headline: Issued suspensions to Mexi Town and Panda Buffet and approved a restaurant all alcohol license for Momo Palace.
summary: The Commission found violations at Mexi Town, Panda Buffet, and Maya Lounge. It issued suspensions to Mexi Town and Panda Buffet and kept Maya Lounge under suspension until its liquor license transfer is completed. It also approved several one-day event and common victualer licenses and continued or postponed other items.

19. Dubai Restaurant & Lounge, Inc. dba Mexi Town, 105 Water Street 
Violation of Rules #14, #16 and 204 CMR 2:05
Lissette Rodriguez appeared to answer to the violation and waived her right to counsel.  Sgt. Needham 
presented the following: 
 
On April 3, 2026, members of the Alcohol Beverage Control Commission and the Worcester Police 
Department Alcohol Enforcement Unit went to Dubai Restaurant & Lounge dba Mexi Town to conduct a 
compliance check. 
 
Upon approaching the premises. the investigators observed a large line of patrons waiting to enter the 
Licensed Premises. Stanchions were located at the main door monitored by security personnel and it was 
immediately apparent that staff were not controlling the flow of patrons waiting to gain entry. The front 
entrance/exit was noticeably blocked making it a safety concern in an event of an emergency. 
 
As investigators entered, they were met by a female who was monitoring the cover charge for patrons. The 
female was identified as Olivia Vanagel and was not an employee of the premises but was a friend of the 
person hosting the party.  
 
Located inside the entrance of the Licensed Premises was a cash box, Venmo & Cash App. QR-Code with 
Ms. Vanagel’s information. Ms. Vanagel informed Sergeant Thomas Needham that the cover charge was 
$15 per person to enter. 
 
Officer Patrick Harrington made his way to the rear of the premises and observed dinner tables pushed 
towards the outer walls, low lighting, extremely loud music, dancing by patrons and little to no food. It was 
clear that this was nightclub activity and not a typical restaurant setting.  
 
Officer Harrington was met by staff and due to the loud music went to the kitchen area to speak. Staff were 
advised of the situation, and it was also noted the kitchen area was not active and the equipment was turned 
off, indicating no food service. While within the kitchen area a strong order of something burning was 
detected. A further investigation revealed a lit hookah within rear prep area.  This premises is not permitted 
for indoor smoking.  
 
Staff were advised to contact the manager of record, but were unsuccessful. 
 
It should be noted that on March 27, 2026, the staff at the premises were previously advised that their 
license is for restaurant use and not a night club. At that time, they were given instructions if they wished to 
pursue a nightclub license designation they would need to apply for a change in use and follow all state and 
local rules and regulations.  
 
Ms. Rodriguez stated that they did have a promoter that night and they were not aware that was going to 
happen. Ms. Rodriguez with regard to the hookah that was an employee who is no longer with the premises 
as that is not allowed. 
 
Sgt. Needham stated that the evening staff of the Licensed Premises was present and was aware that a cover 
charge was being collected.  
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 that the violation did occur. 
 
The Commission noted that there was a three day suspended suspension on record from December 2025.
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 that the violation did occur.  
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to issue the three day suspended suspension as well as a 
five day suspension with three days to be served. The six days to be served are July 24, 25, 26, 29, 30, 
31. The remaining two days will remain on the licensee’s record from a year from the hearing date any if 
any further violations occur the two days will be served along with any suspension the Commission 
imposes. 
 
List of Exhibits:  Police report dated April 20, 2026. 
 
20. BMW Group, Inc. dba Panda Buffet, 97 Stafford Street 
Violation of Rule #14 
 
Attorney Bornstein and Xueyun Lin appeared upon behalf of the violation. 
 
Sgt. Needham presented the following; 
 
 
On February 08, 2026, at approximately 1800 hours First Half Operations Officers were dispatched to 
Brookline St. for a reported Indecent Assault and Battery. Upon arrival they spoke with an identified 
victim who stated she was an employee at Panda Buffet located at 97 Stafford St. She stated that while 
at work this evening she and another male employee who she only knows as “Barry” were cleaning in a 
secluded area of the dining room. She stated that the male employee waived her over to him at which 
time he grabbed her arms and the back of her head and attempted to kiss her. The victim was able to 
break away from him, at which time the male grabbed her breast area. The victim immediately notified 
the Manager, known to the victim as “Winnie”, of the indecent assault and battery. The manager of the 
business later identified as Xue Yun Lin was on scene working in her capacity as manager that evening. 
The victim then left the restaurant and went home. Once the victim got home, she called the police and 
returned to the restaurant with her father. There were no calls to Worcester Police Dispatch from the  
business or Ms. Lin reporting the incident as required by Rule 14 after being made aware of the assault 
and battery.  
 
Operations officers spoke to Lin in an attempt to obtain information on the male employee involved. She 
stated that the male who she knows as “Barry” was fired and was no longer on scene. She stated she 
couldn’t provide any other information on him because he had only been working there for a few days. 
Officers attempted to access the interior cameras of the restaurant but were told by management that 
only the owners can access them and they live in New Hampshire. A report was filed and forwarded to 
the Sexual Assault Unit.  
 
On February 20, 2026, Officer Glenn Stout assisted Detective Joseph Ford with a follow up regarding 
the incident that occurred on February 08, 2026. Upon arrival we asked the hostess to speak with the 
Manager. We were told he was in the bathroom, and he would be right out. Approximately 20 minutes 
later Colby Yang met with us. Detective Ford asked him if there was a place we could talk, Mr. Yang 
brought us over to the hostess station. Detective Ford asked him if he had an office someplace a little 
more private, he stated yes and walked us into a walk in storage closet at the back of the restaurant. 
Officer Stout asked Mr. Yang again if there was an office we could go to. He finally escorted us through 
the kitchen to the business office.
Inside the office, we observed the CCTV system and monitors all appeared to be operating. We also 
observed a number of filing cabinets. Colby Yang stated he was not an employee at the restaurant, but 
he was just filling in for Xue Yun Lin who was currently in China. Mr. Yang was aware of the incident 
that occurred on February 08, 2026. He stated that the male employee involved was from New York and 
had been fired. He couldn’t provide the employee’s information or the video evidence to us.  
 
Yang was able to contact Lin by phone. Officer Stout spoke with Xue Yun Lin via cell phone. Lin stated 
that she couldn’t retrieve the suspect’s information or the video due to her not being in the country. She 
stated her partner, who she identified as “Jess” could help us. “Jess” was later to be identified as Xiao 
Yan Lin. Xiao Lin is listed as the Vice President and partner with Xue Yun Lin. Officer Stout spoke 
with Xiao Yan Lin via cell phone. Officer Stout explained to her that we needed the suspect/employee 
information of the male involved in the incident on February 08, 2026, and we also needed the video 
evidence from their CCTV system. She stated she was sick and couldn’t come to the restaurant, but she 
could get us the employee information and video and email Detective Ford the next day. Detective 
Joseph Ford received the email containing the requested information the next day from Xue Yun Lin.  
 
It should be noted that on the night of the incident, Xue Yun Lin (Manager) was working and the 
employee information and video evidence requested by the initial responding patrol officers would have 
been available for her to provide. Had Lin provided the requested information on the night of the 
incident, it would have expedited the investigation. The video evidence that was given to Detective Ford 
from “Jess” on Saturday February 20, 2026, was scheduled to be automatically overwritten by the 
CCTV recording system on Monday February 22, 2026. The inaction of Xue Lin on the night the 
incident was reported, could have possibly resulted in the loss and inability to retrieve any video 
evidence pertinent to the indecent assault allegation, therefore potentially impacting the thorough 
investigation of the incident. Fortunately, this was not the case and after further investigation by 
Detective Ford, criminal complaints for Indecent Assault and Battery have been requested against the 
former employee. 
 
Officer Wesley Lojko stated that he took the report at 97 Stafford and after speaking with the victim he 
want to Panda Buffet and attempt to obtain some suspect information and when he went to the restaurant 
he spoke with Ms. Lin she stated she couldn’t provide name or date of birth or any information that 
could identified the male as he only worked there for a handful days. Officer Lojko asked if he could 
access the video footage and Ms. Lin stated that she couldn’t retrieve that the video evening. 
 
Sgt. Needham stated that after the incident Officer Stout and Officer Ford contacted the license holder 
and were able to obtain the video. 
Attorney Bornstein stated that he had viewed the video of the incident and described it as very 
disturbing. He said the manager would never want anyone to experience such an unfortunate incident 
and acknowledged that the situation could have been handled better that evening. 
Attorney Bornstein explained that, when the incident occurred, the manager was not informed of what 
had happened and was only told that the staff member had gone home because she was not feeling well. 
He stated that this information should have been communicated more promptly and that the license 
holder has since implemented procedures to ensure that such information is reported immediately.
Attorney Bornstein further argued that the violation cites Rule #14 but does not establish a correlation to 
the sale or service of alcoholic beverages. 
Attorney Vigliotti responded that Rule #14 pertains to the manager's responsibility for the licensed 
premises. He stated that the license holder has taken corrective measures and is working internally to 
ensure that incident reports and other required information are communicated without delay. 
Commissioner Cruz asked whether the staff member who allegedly assaulted the waitress had been 
apprehended. Sgt. Needham stated that the Worcester Police Department was still searching for the 
individual and added that, had the license holder provided the information immediately, the suspect 
might already be in custody. 
Commissioner Cruz also questioned how the employee who allegedly committed the assault was 
terminated if the manager was initially unaware that the incident had occurred. 
Ms. Lin stated that another employee informed her of the incident afterward, at which point she 
terminated the employee involved. Attorney Bornstein added that the assaulted employee's boyfriend 
was also searching for the individual who allegedly committed the assault. 
Attorney Bornstein acknowledged that there had been a clear breakdown in communication and stated 
that the situation should have been handled more effectively when police responded to the premises. 
Commissioners Cruz and Fisher stated that the alleged sexual assault was an egregious incident and 
expressed that the license holder's failure to respond promptly to law enforcement was highly 
irresponsible. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 that the violation did occur. 
 
The Commission noted that the License  Holder has just appeared few months prior on a violation and 
received a warning at that hearing. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to issue a five day suspension with two days served July 
29, 2026 and July 26, 2026.  
 
List of Exhibits:  Police report dated April 2, 2026 
 
 
21. Suveroo, LLC dba Maya Lounge, 5 Saugus Place 
Violation of Rule #14, MGL c.138§23, Rule #14, 204 CMR 2.05, 204 CMR 4.03 
 
Roopali Kummarikuntla and Ashok Kummarikuntla appeared to answer to the violation and waived 
right to counsel. 
 
On May 23, 2026, members of the Worcester Alcohol Enforcement Unit were notified of a possible 
liquor violation at the Licensed Premises. A social media post indicated a “Happy Hour” violation 
(giving alcohol away for free). The Licensed Premises was identified as “Maya Lounge”
The License Commission had received no notification of change of doing business from the 
ownership/management of the Licensed Premisesl. 
 
Sgt. Thomas Needham and Officer Patrick Harrington went to the Licensed Premises and met with 
Daianara Rosario and Luis Abreau. Ms. Rosario identified herself as the manager of the Licensed 
Premises and then explained that she was in the process of purchasing the business and changed the 
name to District Lounge 2-3 weeks ago. During the conversation both parties explained that the City of 
Worcester was already notified of the transfer through her attorney. No application had been received at 
that time by the License Commission. Ms. Rosario further explained that she paid $3800 towards 
renovations of the Licensed Premises, $2700 in attorney fees and $30,000 towards the business that she 
believed was held in escrow by the attorney. 
 
A further check of the current posted liquor license revealed an expired 2025 license. At that time Sgt. 
Needham and Officer Harrington proceeded to make their way outside and encountered a patron 
utilizing an e-cigarette/vape with the main bar area. Staff was advised of the “no smoking” within the 
Licensed Premises. 
 
A check of the Massachusetts Secretary of State’s website showed that a change in the corporation 
structure had taken place which had not been approved by the local Commission or the Alcoholic 
Beverages Control Commission. Additionally, Ms. Rosario was listed recently on a requested transfer of 
the liquor license and is listed as manager with no beneficial interest which contradicts her May 23, 
2026, statements.  
 
Mr. Kummarikuntla stated that the information that had been read into the record was accurate. 
Commissioner Fisher asked Ms. Kummarikuntla how many days per week she is present at the 
premises. Ms. Kummarikuntla responded that she is usually there two days a week. Sgt. Needham stated 
that whenever there has been an incident at the premises, officers have only seen Ms. Kummarikuntla's 
husband present. 
Ms. Kummarikuntla stated that they attempted to sell the business last year, but the sale did not go 
through due to fraud. She further stated that they have since submitted a new transfer application. 
However, she said they do not know why the proposed new owner changed the LLC name or why the 
proposed owners were promoting the new business name on Instagram before the transfer had been 
approved. 
Commissioner Fisher stated that if Ms. Kummarikuntla were regularly present at the premises, she 
would know what was occurring and would have control over the business. 
Commissioner Cruz stated that Ms. Kummarikuntla and Mr. Kummarikuntla appeared to have no 
control over the business. 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 that the violation did occur. 
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 that the license remain under suspension until the 
transfer of the liquor license is completed.
List of Exhibits:  Police report dated June 24, 2026 
 
Communications 
 
Law Department communication dated Jun 25, 2026, re: Time period for notice of violation hearings. 
Filed 
 
Adjournment  
 
Upon a roll call vote the Commission voted 3-0 to adjourn the meeting at 11:58 a.m.
